title: Switching from paper to app headache diaries: costs and consequences for a hospital headache clinic
abstract: Objective: to estimate the clinic costs and consequences of switching from paper to app headache diaries, and the budget impact on injectable preventives. Design: cost-consequence analysis comparing six months before and after the switch, with a three-year budget impact estimate. Results and conclusions will follow the analysis.
introduction: Electronic diaries are more complete than paper, but the costs of switching a clinic and the consequences for the preventive budget are unknown.
methods: About 950 appointment episodes per period; costs of nurse set-up, appointment time and repeat appointments; usable diaries by the consensus definition; bootstrap intervals; budget impact scenarios.
results: No data have been analysed yet. The report will present the cost-consequence table, usable diaries by age and diary type, and the budget impact scenarios.
discussion: The discussion will weigh clinic savings against set-up costs and the drug budget, and say whether paper should remain.
limitations: Before-after comparison; short follow-up after the switch.
conclusion: To be written after analysis; it will not claim effects on headache frequency.
summary: CHEERS-structured draft with results left empty.
